stem: K and L are the parents of M and N, and M is the only sister of N. N is married to O, and P is the son of N and O. O is the daughter-in-law of K. How is M related to P?

per_option_rationale.rationale: M is described as a sister, so M is female. O is the daughter-in-law of K, so O is female; since N is married to O, N is male. M and N are siblings, so M is the sister of P's father N, which makes M the paternal aunt of P.
Mother treats M as P's parent; P's parents are N and O, while M is only N's sister, so M is P's aunt, one step to the side, not directly above.
Sister keeps M in P's own generation; M belongs to the parents' generation as N's sibling, so relative to P she is an aunt, not a sister.
Niece inverts the generation direction, treating M as one generation below P; in fact M is one generation above P, so she is P's aunt.

explanation: Fix the genders first. M is the only sister of N, so M is female. O is the daughter-in-law of K, so O is female, and since N is married to O, N is male. Now place everyone. K and L are the parents of M and N, so M and N are siblings. P is the son of N and O, so N is P's father. M is the sister of P's father N, and M is female, so M is P's father's sister, that is, P's paternal aunt. Therefore M is the aunt of P.

explanation_sections.punchline: N's gender is hidden until 'O is the daughter-in-law of K' makes O female and so N male; then M, N's sister, is P's paternal aunt.
explanation_sections.approach: Archetype move: an in-law label like daughter-in-law silently fixes a gender; use it to gender the spouse, confirm the sibling link, and only then assign the aunt or uncle term across the generation gap.
explanation_sections.lesson: Side relations (aunt, uncle, niece, nephew) hinge on both the generation gap and the gender; pin the gender from the nearest in-law or only-sister clue before naming the term.
explanation_sections.timing: 120-150 seconds. Fastest elimination: Sister is wrong at a glance because M and P sit one generation apart, so no same-generation term can apply.
